$comment: S3264: which ALL_FEATURES records the Wear store boundary confines to the sideload watch build.
wear/config/store-boundary-policy.json (S3178) answers the question for ROUTES, COMPONENTS and
PERMISSIONS; a ledger record names none of the three, so the join between the two files cannot be
derived and is declared here instead. Read by scripts/quality/assert-allfeatures-sync.ps1 check 6,
which requires every id below to carry wearFlavors ['noLegal'] and fails when a category named
here has left the policy's noLegalOnly set - that is the moment a capability came back to the
store artifact and its records have to be re-read rather than silently kept narrow.
The rule the classification applies: a record is listed when the capability's WATCH half is
carried by a route, component or permission the policy confines to noLegal. A record describing
only phone-side rendering or phone-side robustness is not listed, even when its subject is the
watch - the phone build is what 'flavors' already answers for. A phone-bridge record IS listed
when the watch must participate for the capability to exist at all and its watch half is
sideload-only. Such a record keeps its SUPPORT_WEAR_COMPANION gate and carries wearFlavors beside
it: the two fields answer about different modules and validate.ps1 accepts both at once.
Not listed, on purpose - a capability the policy splits rather than excludes. wearFlavors has no
partial value, so a record whose subject keeps its store half (the Apps list, the home sections)
stays absent rather than trading an overclaim for an underclaim.
